Bible credits

We want children and adults to learn the Word and draw near to Jesus — with clear labels and thankful credit. This page is our promise about how Scripture works on the site.

How we use the Bible (our constitution)

Why this site exists: so people can know Jesus Christ, trust His Word, and find life in Him — one honest verse at a time, without noise or performance.

  • KJV is the truth on this site. The King James Version is our primary Scripture: what we quote, memorize, plan from, teach from, and check for accuracy.
  • BBE helps you understand it. The Bible in Basic English is optional simpler English for the same verse — a bridge for kids, new readers, and tired minds. It never replaces the KJV and is never labeled as KJV.
  • Same reference always. If you see KJV John 3:16, any BBE line under it is also John 3:16 — never a different passage.
  • Plain teaching is third. Short “what it means” lines are our porch words, not a Bible translation. They sit under Scripture, not above it.

We build fail-safes and human review so the Word stays accurate. Our hope is that someone meets Jesus here and is saved — not that we win an argument about tools.

Primary Scripture — King James Version (KJV)

Every main verse on Today’s Daily Battle is shown from the King James Version.

The KJV is in the public domain in the United States. We label it KJV so you always know what you are reading.

Credit: King James Version (public domain).

Optional simpler English — Bible in Basic English (BBE)

Where it helps children, new readers, or anyone who wants plainer words, we may offer a second line labeled In simpler words (BBE).

That text is from the Bible in Basic English, a whole-Bible translation that uses a limited, everyday vocabulary. It is offered as a bridge to understanding — not a replacement for the KJV, and never labeled as KJV.

The BBE was printed in 1965 by Cambridge University Press in England without a copyright notice and distributed in America; it is widely treated as public domain in the United States. We are thankful for that gift to the church.

Credit: Bible in Basic English (BBE) — public domain. Originally associated with work overseen by S. H. Hooke and published for plain-English readers; 1965 Cambridge printing treated as public domain in the U.S. We do not claim ownership of the BBE text.

Simple layman terms (our porch teaching)

Simple layman terms on this site are short teaching lines written for Today’s Daily Battle — plain meaning and gentle application, not a full alternate Bible translation. They sit under the KJV and under optional BBE so Scripture wording leads, then a gentle unpacking if you open it.

Order on the page

  1. KJV first — the verse you can trust and share as Scripture here.
  2. In simpler words (BBE) — plain public-domain Bible wording for the same reference (children and new readers).
  3. Simple layman terms — optional short teaching for real life (when you open it).

Our hope is simple: that kids and adults understand the Word, meet Jesus, and take one faithful step — without confusion about sources, and with thanks to those who made free plain-English Scripture available.

Spanish topic pages

Some Spanish mood pages may quote Reina-Valera 1960 or note public-domain Spanish Scripture separately. Those pages say so on the page. The main English Bible tool remains KJV.
